one_liner: Single-threaded SSE2 analytic-coverage 2D path rasterizer in D; claims speed but publishes no comparison with Cairo or Blend2D.
what_it_does: dg2d fills paths built from lines, quadratic and cubic curves into a 32-bit ARGB pixel buffer, with solid colour and linear, radial, angular and biradial gradient paints under non-zero or even-odd winding. The API is a D Canvas class (fill, draw(path, paint, windingRule), viewport and clip state) over a Rasterizer class that hands each finished scanline to a blitter delegate. It also rips glyph outlines from TrueType files into one path. It is not a drop-in for Cairo or Blend2D: there is no stroking, no image or pattern fill and no Porter-Duff blend modes.
how_it_is_fast: The rasterizer computes exact-area (analytic) anti-aliased coverage in 24:8 fixed point and stores it per scanline in differentiated (delta) form, so long spans with constant coverage need no per-pixel work. A bitmask with one bit per 4 pixels marks cells where an edge touches the scanline; the blitters bit-scan that mask to skip empty spans or write opaque spans with plain aligned 16-byte stores, an idea the source credits to Blend2D. Blitters integrate the deltas and blend 4 pixels at a time with SSE2 intrinsics (intel-intrinsics), and edges crossing the left or right clip edge are folded into per-row clip accumulation buffers instead of being tested per pixel.
when_to_use: A D program that needs anti-aliased solid or gradient path fills into its own 32 bpp buffer on x86 without linking a C or C++ graphics library.
Studying a compact (about 1,000-line) delta-coverage scanline rasterizer with a span bitmask before reading Blend2D's much larger code base.
UI or plugin rendering in D where the maintained Dplug fork (dplug:canvas, nothrow @nogc, no alignment requirement) is the real target and dg2d is the upstream reference.
Filling many small shapes or glyph outlines per frame on one core, which is what the demo panels exercise.
when_not_to_use: You need evidence that it beats Cairo or Blend2D: no benchmark, timing table or baseline exists in the repository or its issues, and the demo's FPS readout compares against nothing.
You need stroking, images, pattern fills, transforms on paints, compositing operators or multi-threaded rendering; the README lists all of these as not yet done.

Non-x86 targets or straight-alpha pixel formats: the README requires SSE2, 32 bpp with alpha in the high byte and 16-byte aligned scanlines; the maintainer said ARM testing would need a Linux port that he never did (issue #6).

Production code that needs maintenance: library code last changed on 2020-11-14 (the 2022 commits touch only the demo's X11/XWayland window), the API is declared unstable, and a 2025 angular-gradient bug report is unanswered.
@nogc or betterC code: the Rasterizer and Canvas are GC-allocated classes and the rasterizer's scanline, mask, bucket and clip buffers are GC dynamic arrays.

integration.form: dub package (library target) or source-drop of source/dg2d/*.d
integration.min_toolchain: Not documented; any D compiler with intel-intrinsics 1.x, LDC recommended with link-time optimization or cross-module inlining so the intrinsics inline
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 with SSE2; demo windowing on Win32 and X11; ARM untested
integration.thread_safety: not documented; rendering is single-threaded and each Canvas and Rasterizer holds mutable per-instance state

gotchas: The 16-byte buffer alignment and stride-multiple-of-4 rules are checked only by assert; release builds drop the checks and the blitters use aligned SSE loads and stores (_mm_load_si128/_mm_store_si128), so an external misaligned buffer can fault. Canvas allocates its own pixels with C realloc, which gives 16-byte alignment on common 64-bit allocators but is not guaranteed everywhere.

Angular gradients with RepeatMode.Pad never select one quadrant (fixupQuadrant can produce positions down to about -0.25), so part of the gradient is missing; p0nce posted a one-line SSE fix in issue #13 (2025-04-11) that is not merged.

Coincident edges after clipping once left zero spans in the delta buffer that made blitters skip or solid-fill wrongly (horizontal-line artifacts, issue #2, fixed in dff0979 on 2020-06-03); the delta-integration design means one bad cell corrupts the rest of the scanline. Copying a Font struct double-freed its data (issue #7); the maintainer's fix was to disable copying.

The demo's FPS figure is the best of 5 timed paints per timer tick, maxed over the last 25 ticks (effectively best of 125), with the canvas clear outside the timed region; it is an optimistic single-core number with no baseline and is not a benchmark.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No rasterizer is catalogued in this category (the siblings are sorters, file tools, allocators and codecs); among catalogued rasterizers Blend2D (wave 10, tier B) and tiny-skia (tier A) have measured numbers and more features, so pick dg2d only for a D-native, dependency-light fill rasterizer, and prefer its maintained Dplug fork for real use.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing was measured: the README says only 'Very fast, high performance rasterizer with SIMD support' and that LDC with LTO or cross-module inlining performs best, the lead's 'about 2x Cairo' appears nowhere, and issue #8 discusses glyph speed against GDI without timings while the maintainer estimates a possible 4x glyph speedup from caching.
status_note: Abandoned (library code unchanged since 2020-11-14, last commit 2022-05-06 on the demo, 21 stars) but BSL-1.0 and small enough to vendor; its rasterizer lives on, reworked as nothrow @nogc without alignment requirements, in Dplug's dplug:canvas, which is the better-maintained copy.
